rounds.text: Jai Corp Ltd is fundamentally undervalued, trading at a compelling price-to-earnings ratio of 10.9x based on filed statements [E1], which sits at a steep discount to the sector benchmark P/E of 25.21x [E6]. This attractive valuation is further underscored by a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.32x (at a price of ₹ 103 against a book value of ₹ 78.3) [E2], compared to a sector benchmark P/B of 2.23x [E7]. Profitability is remarkably robust, highlighted by a stellar return on assets (ROA) of 10.86%, which significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of -2.72% [E8]. Operational efficiency is also gaining strong momentum, evidenced by a quarterly operating margin expanding to 14% in March 2026 compared to 9% in the year-ago quarter [E31], alongside an impressive 36.8% CAGR profit growth delivered over the last 5 years [E62]. Furthermore, profit growth recently exceeds 1-year price growth by 205%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E58]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10 years is -2% [E14], compounded sales growth over 3 years is -5% [E16], and sales declined -12% YoY [E74].

Jai Corp Ltd is significantly under-appreciated because it trades at an exceptionally modest P/E ratio of 10.9x [E1] and 10.54x against a sector benchmark of 25.21x [E6]. This valuation disconnect is further underscored by a price-to-book ratio of just 1.2x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.23x [E7], even while the company achieves a robust return on assets (ROA) of 10.86% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of -2.72% [E8]. Fundamental operational efficiency is visibly improving, evidenced by quarterly operating margins expanding to 14% in March 2026 compared to 9% in the year-ago quarter [E31] and supported by signals of expanding margins [E71] and QoQ sales increases [E70]. Conceded: the long-term sales growth has been poor, with compounded sales growth over 10 years at -2% [E14], 5 years at 1% [E15], 3 years at -5% [E16], and trailing twelve months at -2% [E17].
